verdict.rationale: OpenClaw is itself a personal AI assistant: you chat with it after onboarding and hand it tasks from chat channels. It acts on those tasks through documented tools for shell exec, browser control, computer use, sub-agents and swarms, and scheduled automations or standing orders. Community users report delegating real work to it, such as home IT chores and running nine agents with scheduled tasks; one commenter's general claim that it never did what it should is not a concrete documented failure, so it lowers confidence slightly rather than creating a dispute. Missing for 10: independent evidence of consistent task-completion reliability (hands-on reports are mixed).
